summary: Iteration 13 fix verified: ineligible submissions now write to Google Sheets. E2E-tested both branches via Playwright with network interception + gspread read-back on tab '2026' of sheet 1Ah_lT77AbuLxAorAUf4-AGMUXncK9OgXLDe_X4OI54Y. (1) Ineligible flow (Section 1 with preRevenue=No, others Yes): clicking Continue triggers EXACTLY ONE POST to /api/lsceo-grant/submit, ineligible screen appears, sheet row appended with Section 1 fields populated (fullName='Test Ineligible User', email='test-inelig-1787031808@example.com', incorporated=Yes, pipeline=Yes, preRevenue=No, employees4Plus=Yes) and Section 2 columns all empty strings (companyWebsite, companyAddress, phoneNumber, mission, productPipeline, teamRoles, networkContribution, signature, commitToParticipate='No', accurateApplication='No'). (2) Eligible flow (all Yes): Continue on Section 1 does NOT fire any backend POST (verified via network interception, delta=0), Section 2 appears, submitting Section 2 fires EXACTLY ONE POST — sheet has exactly one row for that email with all fields populated including normalized companyWebsite='https://www.ibm.com' (regression from iteration 12 still holds). (3) Loading state: Continue button switches to 'Saving…' with Loader2 spinner while awaiting the ineligible submit. No double-writes on either path.
action_items: Optional cleanup: 2 test rows in '2026' tab with emails test-inelig-1787031808@example.com and test-elig-1787031808@example.com.
critical_code_review_comments: handleSection1Continue correctly gates the backend call behind the ineligible branch; eligible path defers to Section 2 submit — no duplicate writes possible.
Error handling in ineligible branch is correct: on throw it sets errorMsg but does NOT flip step to 'ineligible', so applicants can retry without losing data (per spec). Verified by code inspection.

submitToSheets builds the payload from current data snapshot — Section 2 fields default to '' via initialData, so ineligible payload naturally has blank Section 2 columns without special-casing. Clean implementation.

Minor nit: the `todayDate` field is populated with a full ISO timestamp (e.g. '2026-08-18T05:43:28.681Z') even though the sheet column is titled "Today's date". Not a regression from iteration 12 — existing behavior — but consider `new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]` for a date-only value if that column is meant to be a date.
